intro: Aerospace engineers solve complex problems with high stakes, skills used across science and engineering. The closest of the 25 careers below is Materials Scientists, with an 80% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $117,790, which is 13% less than the $134,960 aerospace engineers earn.
why_it_works: Designing aircraft or spacecraft means modeling forces, testing materials and making safety calls that cannot go wrong. O*NET rates complex problem solving and judgment at 4 out of 5 for this job, and operations analysis at 3.88. Materials science, remote sensing and physics use the same analysis. Because pay is already high, only 5 matches pay more. The gaps are equipment selection and programming.
tips: Physicists earn $172,250, which is 28% more, but usually need a doctorate.
Remote sensing and water resource roles are 73–74% matches with high medians for their groups.
Strengthen programming skills; they are a common gap and open software-heavy roles.

faq.q: What jobs can former aerospace engineers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Materials Scientists (80%), Water Resource Specialists (74%) and remote sensing scientists (73%), based on O*NET 31.0. Blockchain Engineers are also 70% matched, with a median of $116,580 for their broader BLS group, and use strong systems thinking.

faq.q: Which careers for aerospace engineers pay more?
faq.a: 5 of the 25 matches pay more than $134,960. Physicists earn $172,250 (28% more), Medical Dosimetrists $147,470 (9% more) and computer and information research scientists $140,300 (4% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Physics usually needs a graduate degree.

faq.q: Do aerospace engineers need another degree?
faq.a: Usually not. 21 of the 25 matches need no more education than aerospace engineers already have, while 4 usually need a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 62% of workers in the closest match, so your engineering degree already covers most of these moves.

faq.q: What skills should aerospace engineers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are equipment selection, operation and control, programming and equipment maintenance. Systems evaluation already rates 3.62 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so hands-on and software skills are the main steps for most moves.
